Definition: from G3844 and teino (to stretch); to extend along, i.e. prolong (in point of time):--continue.
BiblicalUsage: Parateino means to stretch out, to prolong. It appears once, in Acts 20:7, where Paul preaches at Troas and continues his speech until midnight, while the believers break bread and Eutychus falls asleep in the window.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a sermon stretched to midnight is worth it when the preacher must leave in the morning, and the church stayed because the word mattered more than sleep.
